title: Congress Tells Modi to Stop 'Sermonising' After BJP Loses Both Varanasi Seats in MLC Polls
excerpt: Jairam Ramesh said voters from Varanasi to Patna had passed a 'no-confidence motion' against the Prime Minister's policies, hitting back at Modi's jibe over Congress's showing in Legislative Council elections across four states.
body:
• Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday over his taunt about the party's MLC election showing.
  • The BJP lost both Legislative Council seats in Varanasi, the Prime Minister's own parliamentary constituency; the Samajwadi Party won them, including the Varanasi Teachers' seat.
  • In Uttar Pradesh's 11 MLC seats, the BJP won six and the SP five; the NDA swept all four seats in Karnataka, which had prompted Modi's original jibe.
  • Ramesh tied the results to inflation, youth unemployment and stalled private investment, calling them a 'no-confidence motion' against the government's policies.

The Congress on Thursday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his taunt at the opposition party's showing in the MLC elections, saying he must stop trolling and sermonising others and instead reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi.

Congress general secretary in charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said that from Varanasi and Nagpur to Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna, the people have clearly passed a "no-confidence motion against" the Prime Minister's policies, according to PTI's report.

"The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's sermonising others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?"

— Jairam Ramesh, Congress general secretary (communications)

What prompted the exchange

Modi had commented on October 28 on the elections for 28 Legislative Council seats held across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka — polls for graduates' and teachers' constituencies, which are decided by limited electorates of graduates and teachers rather than the general public. The Prime Minister's jibe followed an NDA clean sweep in Karnataka, where the alliance won all four seats. Across the four states, the BJP and its NDA partners took the larger share of the 28 seats.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2115685837317009608

The opposition's counter rests on the map's symbolism rather than the overall tally. In Uttar Pradesh, of the 11 seats contested — five graduates' and six teachers' constituencies — the BJP won six and the Samajwadi Party five, including Varanasi and Agra. SP candidate Lal Bihari Yadav secured the Varanasi Teachers' seat, and Congress pointed to its own win in Nagpur, the RSS's home city.

The opposition widens the attack

"Mr. Modi, stop the trolling. Crores of families are reeling from back-breaking inflation, the youth are unemployed, and private investment has ground to a halt," Ramesh said, urging the Prime Minister to drop what he called arrogance and reflect on those issues.

Other opposition voices went further. Congress leader Ajay Rai claimed the BJP was "completely cornered" in the Uttar Pradesh results and alleged that Modi's 2024 Lok Sabha victory from Varanasi was secured through malpractice — an allegation the BJP has not been given cause to answer in this exchange and which remains a claim, not a finding. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, in a post on X reported by ANI, also accused the BJP of electoral malpractice and said the opposition's PDA alliance had delivered a blow to the ruling party; Congress MP Akhilesh Prasad Singh separately called the MLC polls an "election of money" that should be stopped.

What it signals

MLC graduates' and teachers' polls are narrow-electorate contests and are weak predictors of assembly outcomes. But the Varanasi result gives the opposition a pointed talking point — defeats in the Prime Minister's own constituency and in Nagpur — while the NDA retains the stronger overall numbers from the round, including the Karnataka sweep. Both sides are treating the results as material for the larger argument about the economy and incumbency that will run into the next state election season.
